findings.title: The refusal_events verification arm is still not pinned against a predicate change: two new semantically meaningful mutants survive BOTH covering cases, one of them reporting a CLEAN purge over surviving tenant rows
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Both survivors were inspected before confirmation, and each was measured against BOTH covering cases rather than one. M1 appended `AND occurred_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'` to the refusal_events arm (fcdf7603a694 -> e97831a871bc). NOT equivalent: `occurred_at` is this table's single retention clock (migration 116), so the mutant stops counting every Refusal older than the window while those rows survive — a must_be_absent table reporting a CLEAN purge over surviving account decision history, which is the exact failure class RT-17 named. Not on an unexecuted branch either: the arm is the only statement either case runs for this table, and the baseline for both cases was green with exactly one test executed. It survived the new live-DB case because seedRefusalEvent hard-codes NOW() for occurred_at (offboarding-lifecycle.integration.test.ts:658), so both fixture rows sit inside any plausible window; it survived the mock case because that case's four guards are toContain('WHERE account_id = ?::uuid'), not.toContain('business_id'), not.toContain('account_businesses') and values deep-equal [accountId] — an added conjunct that names no new column and binds no new parameter trips none of them. M2 appended `OR account_id IS NOT NULL` (-> 076c7f293624). Also not equivalent: it widens the count to every tenant's rows, so verification can never pass once any other account holds a Refusal and finalizePurgeInTransaction would terminalize every offboarding. It survived the live case because the table held exactly the two rows the case seeds — confirmed COUNT(*) = 0 immediately before the run — and survived the mock case for the same text-shape reason. THE ROOT CAUSE IS THE FIXTURE, NOT THE ARM: the new case seeds exactly two rows, both fresh and both in-tenant, and asserts exactly their count, so any predicate BOTH rows satisfy is invisible to it; and it never purges the account, so it cannot distinguish 'counts rows that exist' from 'detects rows that survived a purge'. BUDGET DISCLOSURE: T1's two-mutation cap was reached with M1 and M2, so this pass produced no KILL for the new case and therefore did not itself demonstrate that the case can fail; that RT-17's two original mutants are killed is established analytically in RT-21's remediation and in RT-17's disposition, not by a run in this pass.

Six mutants re-measured against it, all killed (see INV-01). The wider scope this finding records — 31 must_be_absent tables against 3 live-DB verification arms — is unchanged code and is NOT addressed here.
